title: Fly-half Smith fit to steer England against Wallabies
article_text:
Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury and will start for England in their opening Test of the autumn against Australia on Sunday.

Smith has started England's past five matches at 10, but was a doubt to face the Wallabies in the Nations Championship encounter after coming off late on in Northampton's defeat by Leicester on 24 October.

The 24-year-old is joined in the England XV by flanker Ben Curry, who makes his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months.

Curry, whose twin brother Tom had an injury setback in training earlier this week that took him out of contention, is seen as key to combating Australia's breakdown specialists Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano and ensuring a supply of quick ball to Smith and his backline.

Smith will have Saints team-mate Tommy Freeman as an attacking outlet and a target for crossfield kicks on the wing, while full-back George Furbank, who can step in at first receiver, played alongside both before his summer move to Harlequins.

Alex Coles, another Northampton player, wins a starting second-row spot ahead of George Martin, while Henry Slade is chosen at outside centre, with no space for either Joe Marchant or Will Joseph in the matchday 23.

Fin Baxter, who only made two appearances since a comeback from a 10-month foot-injury lay-off, is the starting loose-head prop, with Ellis Genge poised on the bench alongside Will Stuart, another welcome front-row returnee.

A strong replacement front row was key to England swinging the match their way in a 25-7 win last year, the teams' most recent meeting.

Exeter back row Greg Fisilau is poised to win his first cap after being named on the bench.

After facing the Wallabies, England take on Japan and New Zealand on 14 and 21 November before a Nations Championship finals weekend play-off against an as-yet-undecided southern-hemisphere opponent.

England's squad for the autumn only assembled on Monday evening, while Australia have played seven Tests since their opponents' last outing, a victory over Argentina in July.

"Australia are a talented side who have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months. We know the challenge that awaits us and we're looking forward to it," said England head coach Steve Borthwick.

Borthwick will hope Plymouth-born Exeter star Fisilau, who was first called up to the senior squad in January and whose father Keni represented Tonga, can bring some of the heavy-duty ball carrying lost by Tom Willis' departure to French club rugby.

"[Fisilau has] worked incredibly hard to get to this point and has earned his opportunity through the way he's performed for Exeter and in our training environment," said Borthwick.

"He's a powerful, athletic player who brings real energy to the team."

England are playing at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium for the first time since February's 42-21 defeat by Ireland and are in need of a strong campaign to propel them towards next year's Six Nations and Rugby World Cup.

Australia have named Jeremy Williams, more usually a second row, at blindside flanker as they target England's set-piece.

Elsewhere Len Ikitau, who spent last season at Exeter, returns at inside centre after missing the defeat by New Zealand under the head injury assessment protocols.

Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, who enjoyed a winning Test debut in this fixture two years ago, is named on the wing, while there is plenty of power on the bench to take on England's replacements with Rob Valentini, Taniela Tupou and Carlo Tizzano biding their time on the sidelines.

title: Bok star Faf de Klerk set for extended spell on the sidelines
article_text:
Faf de Klerk has been ruled out for the remainder of the year after the Toyota Cheetahs issued a medical update on their sidelined Bok star.

The double World Cup winner suffered an ankle injury in last month’s 29-27 defeat to Bayonne in the opening round of the Challenge Cup and it has now been confirmed by his club that he won’t play again until January.

In a statement, the Cheetahs said: “Faf de Klerk sustained an ankle injury during the game against Bayonne on 18 October and will be on the sidelines for 8 weeks. He is expected to return in early January, in time for Round 3 of the EPCR Challenge Cup, when the Toyota Cheetahs face Zebre Parma in Italy.

De Klerk was integral to the Cheetahs’ run to the semi-finals of the Currie Cup campaign, which preceded tbe start of the Challenge Cup campaign, following his summer move from the Canon Eagles in Japan.

As a result of his injury, de Klerk will miss the Cheetahs’ debut at their new European home ground, the second round Challenge Cup fixture against Dragons at St Helen’s in Swansea, on 13 December.

Marco Jansen van Vuren and Erich Visser will shoulder the burden at scrum-half in his absence.

The 35-year-old won the last of his 60 Springbok caps in a 55-10 win against Georgia in July last year, although he did feature against the Barbarians in a non-cap game in June.

title: Ellis Genge dropped: Confirmed England team to play Australia
article_text:
Steve Borthwick has made two bold selection calls as England have confirmed their team to face Australia.

The clash will be the first of four autumn internationals for England as they continue their preparations for the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Australia visit on Sunday, before Japan and the All Blacks arrive at Allianz Stadium. England will then host the Nations Championship finals weekend at the same venue.

However, pressure is mounting on Borthwick following a disappointing Six Nations campaign, which saw England record just one victory.

Another underwhelming autumn could leave the head coach facing serious questions over his future.

Borthwick has made two significant gambles when selecting his side.

The first involves a 6-2 split on the bench, with Henry Pollock providing cover for starting wingers Tommy Freeman and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso.

Pollock's physical attributes could make him a dangerous option out wide, but his lack of experience in the position makes the decision a considerable risk.

The back-rower has featured on the wing on several occasions, although playing there for an extended period is a different challenge.

England could find themselves exposed if either Freeman or Feyi-Waboso needs to leave the field, particularly with Pollock having limited experience in the position.

Another notable selection decision sees Ellis Genge dropped to the bench, with Fin Baxter expected to start at loosehead prop.

The decision could be part of Borthwick's plan to introduce Genge later in the match, allowing the experienced prop to provide additional power and impact against tiring opposition.

The remainder of the squad is largely as expected, with George Furbank and Henry Slade reportedly set to start at fullback and outside centre respectively.

Fin Smith is also believed to be fit and available at fly-half, although his potential involvement could raise concerns among supporters.

There are fears that rushing the Northampton Saints playmaker back into action could aggravate his injury and leave him facing a longer spell on the sidelines.

England are expected to officially announce their squad this afternoon, with the reported selections offering an early indication of Borthwick's plans for the Australia clash.

title: Jannik Sinner: Coach Darren Cahill to leave Italian's side at end of 2026
article_text:
The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year.

Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament.

But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks.

Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings.

He is set to return to action at the Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia next month.

Swede Magnus Norman, the long-time coach of recently retired Stan Wawrinka, will join Sinner's team for next season.

"Darren has been an incredibly important part of my journey," Sinner said.

"Together with Simone and the whole team, we have achieved things I dreamed of growing up.

"He has helped me grow both as a player and as a person, and his guidance will stay with me throughout my career."

Cahill had originally planned to leave at the end of 2025, but told Sinner at Wimbledon that the Italian could decide whether he stayed on - as long as he won the title.

"Working with Jannik has been a special honour and privilege," Cahill said.

title: McReight to earn 50th cap as Kiss backs youth in Wallabies lineup for England
article_text:
Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has opted for Declan Meredith at fly-half for their Nations Championship clash against England at Allianz Stadium.

Recent John Eales Medalist Fraser McReight will bring up 50 caps for the Wallabies at Twickenham, named alongside Jeremy Williams and captain Harry Wilson in the back row.

Wallabies prop Angus Bell returns after missing the Bledisloe Cup defeats, starting on the loosehead side with Billy Pollard at hooker and Allan Alaalatoa at tighthead.

It’s an all-Queensland Reds partnership in the second row, with Josh Canham and Lukhan Salakai-Loto rounding out the tight-five.

Ryan Lonergan is trusted at halfback, with Meredith getting the nod in the all-important fly-half role after a promising performance in Sydney against the All Blacks.

Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Max Jorgensen provide firepower on either wing, with the ever-reliable Tom Wright at fullback. Arguably Australia’s best player, Len Ikitau, also returns to the starting lineup having missed the majority of the Bledisloe Cup series, partnering Isaac Henry in the midfield.

Taniela Tupou and Rob Valetini headline a strong bench, which includes Tate McDermott, Ben Donaldson, and Filipo Daugunu as the backline replacements.

“The entire squad has travelled well and prepared with fantastic energy and excitement heading into this weekend,” the Wallabies head coach said.

“Playing England on their home turf – at an iconic venue like Twickenham – is a massive challenge and another great opportunity for us to test ourselves against world-class opposition and keep building our game.”

The Wallabies currently sit in third place in the Southern Hemisphere Nations Championship table with eight points from three Tests.

Kiss’ side will then travel to Edinburgh to take on Scotland, before taking on Wales in Cardiff a week later, prior to the finals weekend in London.

title: George Furbank ends 2-year England exile as Smith gets thumbs up
article_text:
Fin Smith has passed a late fitness test on the calf injury he sustained in Northampton’s derby defeat by Leicester last month and will lead England’s attack against Australia at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.

Smith has established himself as England’s first-choice 10 this year and it will come as a relief to head coach Steve Borthwick that the Saints man has pulled through.

With club teammate, Alex Mitchell, sidelined with a hamstring injury, Smith is partnered at half-back by Jack van Poortvliet, while the centre combination is made up of Seb Atkinson and Henry Slade.

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, England’s most dangerous attacker in the first leg of the Nations Championship, has had his own fitness concerns of late but is named on the left wing, while the prolific Tommy Freeman retains his place on the right edge.

Following his good form for new club Harlequins, George Furbank wins back the No.15 jersey to earn his 15th cap and his first for nearly two years.

Furbank’s last appearance for England was against Japan in November 2024, whilst a Saints player.

While Furbank’s inclusion at full-back at the expense of Marcus Smith is the only change to the backline that started England’s last Test, the chaotic 31-24 win against Argentina in Santiago del Eestero, Borthwick has made three alterations to his starting pack.

The fit-again Fin Baxter is preferred to Ellis Genge at loose-head, Maro Itoje comes into the engine room following his summer off, with George Martin moving to the bench, while Ben Curry steps into openside in the absence of Guy Pepper.

Uncapped Exeter Chiefs back-row forward Greg Fisilau is named among the replacements with England opting for a 6-2 split on the bench.

The Round 4 fixture of the inaugural Nations Championship sees England begin a run of four consecutive matches at Allianz Stadium.

“Australia are a talented side who have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months. We know the challenge that awaits us and we’re looking forward to it,” said Borthwick.

“We’re excited to be playing in front of our home supporters and to start an important block of games. This will also be our last opportunity to face southern hemisphere opposition at home before the World Cup next year.”

On Fisilau’s potential England debut, Borthwick added: “We’re all absolutely delighted for Greg. He’s worked incredibly hard to get to this point and has earned his opportunity through the way he’s performed for Exeter and in our training environment. He’s a powerful, athletic player who brings real energy to the team.”

Following the Australia fixture, England will face Japan and New Zealand at Allianz Stadium in Rounds 5 and 6, before Finals Weekend from Friday 27 to Sunday 29 November.

title: Money-making Nations Championship project carries a cost for fans and players
article_text:
It was a loose kick, tumbling aimlessly end over end into the All Blacks’ half. Their wing Billy Wallace gathered it and sprinted into midfield, through a gap and on into the Welsh half, only their full-back ahead of him now, and with his teammate Bob Deans in the corner of his eye, coming on the inside calling for the ball. Wallace gave the pass and Deans was away, making straight for the posts, tackled at the last moment by Rhys Gabe, and the two of them went sliding for the try‑line together. The ball finished in the tips of Deans’s fingers, at the end of his outstretched arm.

Over the line? On the line? Inches away from the line?

No one knows. The referee John Dewar Dallas insisted that Deans never made it. The match finished 3-0 to Wales: the All Blacks’ solitary defeat in 35 games on their 1905 autumn tour of Europe. Lloyd Jones wrote a great novel about that tour, Carl Nixon turned it into a successful play, Nigel Wray paid £180,000 for the jersey the All Blacks captain Dave Gallaher wore on the day. You can still buy a DVD of a “dramatic reconstruction” of the match, and a century later two Kiwi journalists published a book offering what they considered new, definitive proof about what happened.

Some 121 years later, if you ever want to start an argument, you can walk into the backroom of any Welsh rugby pub and tell the first old boy at the bar that of course Deans scored. Or walk into any Kiwi rugby club bar and say you’re sure he never did.

There are no autumn tours this year. Instead we have the conclusion of the new Nations Championship, starting in Dublin when Ireland play Argentina on Friday night. It’s a tournament designed to provide a context that was apparently lacking in that legendary match between Wales and New Zealand.

Over the next three weekends France, Ireland and Italy all have matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa. England, Scotland and Wales play Australia, Japan, and New Zealand, and at the end there are six games in three days across a long weekend at Twickenham, sixth place in the northern group against sixth in the southern, and so on, all the way until the top two teams play each other at tea-time on Sunday. The “Hemisphere Shield” will be awarded to whoever comes out top in what is being described as a “Ryder Cup style” competition.

It took the sport the best part of a decade to cobble this competition together. World Rugby first suggested it in 2018, but it took the massive debts left by the Covid pandemic to concentrate minds and get the Six Nations, Sanzaar and all their respective private investors to collaborate on making it happen. After all that time they have ended up with a competition that brings to mind the old line about a camel being a horse designed by committee. God knows the game needs the money, but you have to ask if the organisers needed to give away so much of what people love about the sport to get it.

The Nations Championship has been designed with commercial returns in mind. It is a tournament that seems to have been made almost entirely made for TV. Which is why there are so many compromises. The integrity of the competition wasn’t high on the priorities list, which is why Fiji played their “home” games against Wales in Cardiff, England in Liverpool, and Scotland at Murrayfield in the summer, and Japan were made to stage their own match against Ireland in Australia, to save their opponents an extra trip after a fixture against the Wallabies. Player welfare doesn’t seem to have played much of a part in anyone’s thinking either, so England found themselves flying 25,000 miles to play three fixtures in three weeks on three different continents.

Nor did spectator experience: the whole thing seems to have been designed to deter travelling fans, and risk gate revenue, since the organisers now have to find a way to sell half a million tickets for six fixtures where it won’t be clear who is playing when until six days before kick-off, something they’ve done by offering “support your team” tickets that guarantee you a seat at a match you actually want to watch, regardless of when it’s played. It’s a small mercy that the deal with Qatar has just fallen through so at least we’ve been spared the second edition being staged in the Gulf.

It will work. We’ll all watch. If you love rugby the chances are you were going to tune in for these games anyway. France v South Africa in Paris on a Friday night, England v Australia at Twickenham on a cold autumn afternoon, Scotland v New Zealand on a Saturday at Murrayfield: the truth is these matches don’t need selling, their significance has nothing to do with a competition structure that has been cooked up in the commercial department. It’s enough to make you wonder if the people who sell the sport even really understand why people buy it in the first place.

title: Youth Olympics: Malhan Makes History; Zhang Wins Thriller
article_text:
Riyan Malhan became the first player from the United Arab Emirates to win a gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games after he beat top seed Mady Sow in the men’s singles final in Dakar.

In women’s singles, Zhang Yi Xin made a winning follow-up to World Junior title, overcoming a stirring fightback from India’s Tanvi Patri to prevail in the most exciting match of the competition, 26-24 in the third game.

Sow started strongly, racing to a 10-4 lead before Malhan caught up at the interval. The game was even at 17, after which the UAE player shot ahead with four straight points.

The second game followed the same pattern, with Malhan having to catch up after an early deficit. Sow had the opportunity to take the game as he led 18-16 but once again Malhan was sharper at the end, as he won five straight points for the title.

“Coming into this tournament, I was not fit at all,” Malhan told OIS. “I had very high fever before the matches, but I managed to pull it off, and I’m really happy I could win a gold medal – more than what I expected.”

Women’s singles saw a sensational final between World Junior champion Zhang and Asian U17 champion Tanvi Patri.

After a game apiece, Zhang steamed ahead in the third, holding what appeared to be an unassailable lead at 19-10. Patri then made a sensational comeback, winning 11 of the next 12 points and saving five match points to level at 20.

Patri then had three opportunities to win the gold, but Zhang saved each, and then converted her own seventh match point to win the title.

“The third game was extremely intense. At the beginning, I didn’t make the most of the advantage I had, but I managed to win,” said Zhang.

“I was completely absorbed in the match, and every single point had my full attention. When I won, I didn’t fully realise what had happened. I don’t think I had really registered that the match was over.

“I am very excited because this is a competition that takes place once every four years. Being able to win a medal here is something very special.”

In the playoffs for bronze, Hong Tian Yue (China) beat Park Jung Bin (Korea) 21-17 21-12 in men’s singles, while Yuzuno Watanabe (Japan) beat Cheng Chih-Yun (Chinese Taipei) 21-14 21-8 in women’s singles.

title: Sky Sports Secures Exclusive UK and Ireland Broadcast Rights for Inaugural Women’s TGL (WTGL)
article_text:
Pay-TV broadcaster Sky Sports has secured exclusive live broadcast rights across the UK and Ireland for WTGL, the new tech-focused women’s team golf league launched in partnership with the LPGA Tour and TMRW Sports.

The two-year agreement covers the 2026 and 2027 seasons, expanding Sky Sports’ golf broadcast portfolio alongside a two-year rights extension for the men’s TGL presented by SoFi.

The inaugural WTGL presented by SoFi season launches on 8 November 2026 at the custom-built SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. Every regular-season fixture and the post-season play-offs—scheduled for 20 to 23 December—will broadcast live across Sky Sports platforms. The competition mirror’s the men’s tech-driven format, incorporating mic’d-up players, real-time risk-reward shot decisions, and varied match-play structures within an arena setting.

The league features five founding franchises, each featuring a five-player roster of elite LPGA Tour athletes. Across the 25 total players, the rosters combine for 15 major championship titles and 48 Solheim Cup appearances:

Sky Sports has also confirmed extended rights for the men’s TGL, which expands to seven teams for its third season launching on 27 December 2026 at the SoFi Center. Season three introduces at least 12 new PGA Tour players to the circuit.

Opening night double-header fixtures feature Rory McIlroy’s Boston Common Golf—featuring off-season signing Shane Lowry, facing expansion franchise Motor City Golf Club, led by Brooks Koepka and rising star Jackson Koivun.

The second fixture sees a rematch of last season’s SoFi Cup Finals, with Tiger Woods’ Jupiter Links Golf Club competing against defending champions Los Angeles Golf Club, headlined by Tommy Fleetwood and Justin Rose.

title: GFA says FDA rejection cost Ghana Premier League $5m-a-year Guinness deal
article_text:
Ghana Football Association (GFA) President Kurt Okraku has told Parliament the association lost a sponsorship deal with Guinness Ghana worth more than $5m a year after the countries Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) refused to approve it, and has asked lawmakers to remove the regulator’s power to block alcohol sponsorship in sports.

Speaking before Parliament’s Select Committee on Youth and Sports on Wednesday, November 4, Okraku said the brewer had approached the GFA about a significant investment in the Ghana Premier League.

“We were approached by Guinness Ghana Limited wanting to invest heavily in the Ghana Premier League. We did whatever we had to do. We had a series of meetings. At the end, FDA said no. The deal was, if I’m not mistaken, over $5 million a year. We lost it,” he said.

Okraku did not say when the talks took place. He asked the committee to lead efforts to scrap the provision that requires FDA approval for sponsorships involving alcoholic beverage companies.

“That provision that allows FDA to say yes or no to sponsorship still exists within our books. If there’s one thing that you can do to help sports and football, that would be for you to lead the charge to completely take out that provision,” Okraku added.

The rule sits in the FDA’s guidelines on food advertising, which require any promotion linking an alcoholic drink to a sporting activity to be submitted for the authority’s approval. The same guidelines restrict alcohol advertising on radio and television to between 8pm and 6am, and bar well-known personalities, including sports figures, from endorsing alcoholic drinks. The FDA has defended its approach to alcohol marketing on public health grounds, particularly exposure among minors.

At the GFA’s Congress in August 2025, he said the restrictions had cost Ghanaian football millions of cedis and proposed a framework for responsible alcohol sponsorship, developed with the FDA, the sports ministry, civil society and health groups.

The disclosure puts a figure on a debate that has largely been argued in principle. The rule is an approval requirement rather than an outright ban, so the FDA could change its position without new legislation, through its own guidelines. Okraku’s appeal to Parliament suggests the GFA does not expect that to happen.

Guinness Ghana Breweries came under new ownership in 2025, when Diageo sold its 80.4% stake to France’s Castel Group for $81m. Diageo retained the Guinness brand and still leads its marketing in Ghana with Castel, so the approach to the league came under the new ownership structure.

In the Ghanian Premier League, where clubs have struggled to attract major sponsors, the question is whether lawmakers weigh a recurring eight-figure-cedi commitment (approximately, depending on the exchange rate) against the public health case the FDA has made for its rules. Elsewhere on the continent, brewers remain among football’s most prominent backers, giving the GFA a ready comparison as it makes its argument to lawmakers.

title: Versant’s Fandango, Transmit partner on live sports advertising
article_text:
- Transmit and Fandango have partnered to introduce new advertising opportunities during live sports and entertainment programming.

- The partnership allows advertisers to sponsor key moments during live matches without adding traditional commercial breaks.

- The technology is being used during Bundesliga soccer matches streamed free on Fandango in the United States.

Versant’s Fandango-branded streaming platform has partnered with advertising technology company Transmit to introduce new sponsorship opportunities during live sporting events without adding traditional commercial breaks, the companies announced on Thursday.

The technology is being used during Bundesliga soccer matches streamed on Fandango in the United States, allowing advertisers to place sponsorship messages around significant moments during live competition, Versant said in a statement.

Rather than relying on scheduled advertising breaks, Transmit’s technology identifies events such as substitutions, momentum changes, official reviews and other moments when audience engagement may increase. Advertisers can then place sponsorship messages alongside the live programming without interrupting the game itself.

The partnership is being introduced as Fandango expands its sports programming, including coverage of Germany’s Bundesliga soccer league: Under the league’s U.S. distribution arrangement, USA Sports will carry more than 300 Bundesliga matches during the 2026-27 season. At least 30 matches will air on USA Network, while the remaining games will stream free on Fandango.

“The opportunity in streaming isn’t simply to replicate the traditional television model online. It’s to create entirely new experiences for fans, advertisers, and content partners,” Versant President of Digital Platforms and Ventures Will McIntosh said in a statement.

Transmit CEO Seth Hittman said the technology is intended to identify advertising opportunities as they develop during live events, rather than requiring sponsors to rely on predetermined commercial inventory.

“Everyone understands the value of a FIFA World Cup hydration break,” Hittman said. “It’s one of the most effective sponsorship moments in sports because it’s part of the experience, not an interruption to it. We’re taking that same philosophy and applying it dynamically across live sports. Instead of creating value according to a schedule, we’re identifying it in real time.”

The companies said the approach could generate additional advertising revenue from streaming sports while limiting interruptions to viewers.

Versant was spun out of Comcast’s NBC Universal earlier this year, comprising the company’s former cable networks business (except Bravo, which NBC Universal retained) and digital platforms like Fandango. The company also owns a multicast business called Free TV Networks.

Earlier in the week, Versant said it earned $1.59 billion in overall revenue during the third quarter (Q3) of the year, including $373 million in advertising revenue, down 5.3 percent compared to last year on a carve-out basis.

title: 15-year-old Tanvi Patri scripts history, becomes first Indian woman to win Youth Olympics badminton medal
article_text:
At just 15, Odisha's Tanvi Patri becomes the first Indian woman to win a badminton medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her remarkable silver-medal run in Dakar was a story of composure, courage and extraordinary fighting spirit, highlighted by a stunning comeback in the final against China's reigning World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin.

India's Tanvi Patri scripted a historic chapter in Indian badminton after clinching the silver medal in the women's singles event at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. The 15-year-old from Odisha became the first Indian woman to reach a badminton final and win a medal at the Youth Olympics, marking a significant milestone for the country's junior badminton circuit.

However, the road to the podium was anything but straightforward. Tanvi's campaign was defined by her ability to rise to the occasion, particularly in the knockout stages, where she displayed remarkable composure against some of the tournament's strongest opponents.

The young shuttler eventually settled for silver after an 82-minute battle against China's reigning World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin in the gold-medal match. Tanvi went down 15-21, 21-13, 24-26 in a thrilling three-game encounter, but her spirited fightback in the deciding game ensured that her performance would be remembered long after the final point.

The final against Zhang was a test of Tanvi's temperament and endurance. After losing the opening game 15-21, the Indian bounced back impressively to take the second game 21-13 and force a decider.

The third game, however, appeared to be slipping away from her when she found herself trailing 10-19. With the gold medal seemingly within Zhang's grasp, Tanvi produced an extraordinary response, refusing to surrender despite the mounting pressure.

She saved five consecutive match points to draw level at 24-24, turning what looked like a comfortable finish for the Chinese shuttler into a tense battle. Tanvi even earned three opportunities to seal the gold medal herself, but Zhang held her nerve in the closing exchanges to eventually prevail 26-24.

Although the defeat denied her the gold, Tanvi's determination to fight until the very end stood out as one of the defining moments of the tournament.

The 15-year-old, who trains at the Prakash Padukone Badminton Academy (PPBA), entered the competition as the third seed and enjoyed a strong start in the group stage.

Tanvi faced Thailand's seventh-seeded Kakanik Kungkaew in the quarterfinals, with a place in the medal rounds at stake. The Indian youngster delivered a composed performance, winning 21-17, 21-13 in just 39 minutes. The straight-games victory not only secured her a semifinal berth but also made her the first Indian woman to reach the badminton semifinals at the Youth Olympic Games.

The semifinal against Japan's second-seeded Yuzuno Watanabe proved to be a much tougher examination.

Tanvi began confidently, taking the opening game 21-14 with an aggressive approach and precise shot-making. However, Watanabe responded strongly in the second game, capitalising on Tanvi's errors to level the contest with a 21-11 win.

With a place in the final on the line, the Indian youngster needed to produce her best badminton in the deciding game. She managed to regain control of the rallies, improved her attacking approach and kept her composure in the closing stages.

In a closely contested decider, Tanvi edged past Watanabe 21-19 to book her place in the gold-medal match.

The victory was another landmark moment, making her the first Indian woman to reach a badminton final at the Youth Olympics.

Tanvi's silver medal also adds to India's growing legacy in badminton at the Youth Olympic Games. She joins H.S. Prannoy, who won silver in 2010, and Lakshya Sen, who secured silver in 2018, as Indian badminton players to have reached the podium at the prestigious multi-sport event.

More importantly, her achievement marks a first for Indian women's badminton at the tournament.

title: Rahm and Hatton join Laporta at Abu Dhabi summit - Articles - Rolex Series
article_text:
Ryder Cup team-mates Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton reeled in Francesco Laporta to share the lead heading into the weekend at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

Italian Laporta had led after a brilliant 62 on day one but a 70 in round two at Yas Links left the door ajar and close friends Hatton and Rahm took advantage.

Hatton carded a 65, two shots fewer than Rahm, and the pair will now both head into the weekend at 12 under alongside Laporta looking for a record sixth Rolex Series victory.

Rory McIlroy is hoping to join them to join them on five and he carded a 63 to sit one shot back alongside Pole Adrian Meronk and English pair Sam Bairstow and Matt Jordan.

The Northern Irishman is also hunting an eighth Race to Dubai title and with leader Eugenio Chacarra back on three under, he is well positioned to advanace his cause on that front.

Hatton was a winner of this event in 2021 at Abu Dhabi Golf Club but seems equally at home at Yas Links with a second and two other top tens in four starts.

The Englishman birdied his first two holes and then made four in a row from the sixth to turn in 30.

Further gains followed on the 11th and 13th as he hit the front on his own but a bogey on the 16th dropped him back closer to the pack on a day where several players had held a share of the lead.

"Really happy how I've played," he said. "Obviously, there's been a couple of mistakes. But overall, compared to where I've been at over the last month and a half, it's nice to put a couple of decent scores together again."

Event debutant Rahm went out in the final group of the day and was soon in front with birdies on the second, third and fifth.

He then made four birdies and three bogeys in a roller coaster next seven holes before a two-putt gain on the last put him back on top.

"Pretty good play," he said. "Only thing to take back would be just a couple of bad tee shots right now, feeling fairly comfortable otherwise.

"Just there's been a couple of swings off the tee that were unexpected. But hopefully I can fix that, but otherwise the play has been lovely.

"I'm really looking forward to (the weekend). This part of the world has treated me very well, and I'm hoping I can do on the weekend what I've already done."

Laporta had a roller coaster of his own as he bogeyed the third but then made a hat-trick of birdies from the seventh.

He made a bogey-birdie start to the back nine and while a double on the 14th could have derailed his round, he picked the shots back up on the 15th and last.

"End of the day, it was a good day," he said. "I didn't start very well, I was one over after six. Then I made three birdies in a row, a few mistakes on the back nine, but few really in the last four.

"I'm quite happy about how I finished but still a lot of golf to play."

McIlroy found an unplayable lie as he bogeyed the first but then birdied the second, fourth and seventh and made five in a row from the ninth.

That run ended with a bogey but he would still make gains on three of his last four holes for a total of 11 birdies - his highest in a DP World Tour round.

Meronk and Jordan both carded rounds of 67, one shot fewer than Bairstow, to sit a shot ahead of Spaniard David Puig and Austrian Bernd Wiesberger.

title: Mady Sow claims silver at Dakar 2026

title: WTA takes 'full responsibility' after Pegula 'diva' comment live-streamed
article_text:
The Women's Tennis Association says it takes "full responsibility" for not telling players there were microphones on practice courts after private comments Jessica Pegula made to her coach about fellow player Mirra Andreeva were live-streamed.

The session at Indian Wells, California, was streamed by the WTA before its Tour Finals start on Sunday.

In a private conversation with her coach Mark Knowles, world number five Pegula described Andreeva as "a diva".

The American could also be heard saying the French Open champion "needs to be humbled" and her coach Conchita Martinez encourages her behaviour.

Pegula's agent, Chris McCormack, said she had been "completely unaware" the conversation could be heard by courtside microphones, "let alone live-streamed to the public".

"Naturally it's been an unfortunate situation for everyone involved," McCormack told BBC Sport.

"Jess has since been in direct contact with those involved, which she felt was important to do personally rather than through the media."

YouTube streams of Wednesday's practice sessions at Indian Wells have since been removed by the WTA, but the footage had already been shared on social media.

It is understood the microphones were only intended to capture the sounds of rallies and not any conversations on court, and there will be no audio on future videos.

"The WTA takes full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players' practice, were active on the courts at the WTA Finals," a statement read.

"We sincerely apologise for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed."

Pegula, who is a member of the WTA players' council, also praised Andreeva, saying the world number three is "wonderful" and "smart".

The season-ending WTA Finals, being held at Indian Wells for the first time, run until 15 November.

Pegula's representative and the WTA have been approached for comment.

In a separate incident, world number one Elena Rybakina appeared to have an angry exchange with her coach before a practice session with Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

Some of the audio is unclear, but Pegula can be heard describing how Andreeva and Martinez complained throughout the session, even though Andreeva won every game.

Pegula: "Conchita's always been very nice to me, but I've lost a little respect for her because I'm like, this girl - I think she's a nice girl - she's just a diva. She needs to be humbled. She needs to be [inaudible] putting her in her place; [inaudible] stand up to her."

Spaniard Martinez - the 1994 Wimbledon champion - began working with Andreeva in April 2024. Andreeva reached the Wimbledon quarter-finals last year and claimed her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros in June.

Pegula: "Conchita pokes her and eggs on her behaviour."

Knowles: "She needs somebody to put her in her place. Once she gets that, I think she'll be really good. I mean, she's already really good. Look how she moves."

Pegula: "She moves like a cat. She's wonderful. She's got the perfect serve. She's smart. She anticipates well."

Pegula, who has not won a Grand Slam, then compared Andreeva to world number four Coco Gauff. The American was also 19 when she won her first Grand Slam. Now 22, she has won two majors.

Pegula: "It's so funny how you see her and then you see Coco's mentality. If she had Coco's mentality, she'd be better than her."

Pegula: "The serve, everything, all-around, and she moves just as good. But like mentally, she's..."

Pegula and Andreeva are in different groups at the WTA Finals but could meet in the semi-finals or final.

Pegula's group opponents are Gauff, Rybakina and Noskova, and the latter pair's practice session at Indian Wells was also live-streamed.

Australian and US Open champion Rybakina appears to remonstrate with coach Stefano Vukov as they walk to the net, saying: "Stay here. I'm talking to you. Can you stand here?"

They shared a few more words, which are inaudible, before going to the other side of the court together to greet Noskova and her team.

Vukov was suspended by the WTA in February 2025 following an independent investigation into his behaviour towards Kazakhstan's Rybakina. He returned to her team that August.

Pegula was among the players to complain about additional behind-the-scenes cameras at the Australian Open in January.

The semi-finalist described the filming as an "invasion of privacy" that needs to be "cut back".

"You just feel like you're under a microscope constantly," she said.

title: Zoox doubles down on F1 presence with Las Vegas GP deal

title: Ireland's home straight to World Cup starts with Pumas
article_text:
Los Pumas - two words to strike fear into the heart of Ireland rugby fans.

As they return to the Aviva Stadium in the Nations Championship on Friday night, it feels something of an anomaly that a team who have inflicted so much hurt on Ireland over the years have never beaten them in Dublin.

Indeed, out of the 20 previous meetings between these two sides, Ireland have won 14. It is the nature of those handful of losses, however, that have so coloured this rivalry.

Three times the sides have met at the World Cup.

Three times Argentina have won and three times the result has heralded Ireland's early exit from the competition.

With Ireland's first game of Australia 2027 now just under 11 months away, the sight of the blue and white hoops of their frequent tournament nemesis will certainly sharpen the mind.

All the more so given that, should results go in accordance with seeding, the sides would meet at the quarter-final stage on Halloween night in Brisbane.

As he announced his team selection on Wednesday afternoon, Ireland head coach Andy Farrell acknowledged his side are not presently "good enough to board the plane believing that 100%" they are ready to lift the Webb Ellis trophy for the first time.

A year out from the World Cups of 2015, 2019 and 2023, Ireland had enjoyed banner seasons, and by this stage were eagerly anticipating the tournaments to come.

While that has not been the case through 2026 to date, the head coach added that he is excited by the thought of the work still to do.

If wider optimism around next year feels in short supply, it is because Ireland's issues have come to bear when playing the very best.

Across the past two years, their only six defeats have come in the six games they have played against New Zealand, South Africa and France. All came via double-digit scores.

As such, the eye has long been drawn to the visit of the Springboks to Dublin on 21 November, but there can be no looking past a dangerous Argentina fixture.

The Pumas will be expected to provide a good yardstick for both the collective and a number of individuals in an intriguing selection.

With Jack Crowley injured, Sam Prendergast has another opportunity to grab the 10 jersey. When the then 21-year-old made his debut in this fixture two years ago, it certainly felt like a selection with the future, and the 2027 World Cup, in mind.

The Leinster player has had an uneven start to his Test career, and had lost his place in even his provincial 23 by the time of last season's Champions Cup final, but has the chance to lay down a real marker this month.

Farrell has also put his faith in two regular bench options from the start.

For all the talk of Prendergast's readiness to be Johnny Sexton's long-term successor at fly-half, the now assistant coach's role as the backline's cerebral fulcrum has already been assumed by Jamison Gibson-Park.

Arguably Ireland's most important player during this World Cup cycle, the scrum-half missed the start of the season with a groin injury but was player of the match in his return against Munster at the Aviva Stadium.

He will start this window on the bench with Craig Casey instead getting the nod. The 27-year-old will win his 31st cap on Friday but will be making just a second start against a side currently in the top eight of the world rankings.

It is a similar story for Nick Timoney, preferred here to Josh van der Flier, who has become a trusted bench option over the past 12 months but gets a start against this level of opposition for the first time.

Without Caelan Doris and Jack Conan through injury, how the Ulster flanker, Sean Jansen and Ryan Baird fare against what is an abrasive Argentina back row should have a big impact on the game.

While United Rugby Championship results for Irish sides this season have been poor - the provinces have combined for just six wins, three of them by Leinster - key players should at least be more battle-hardened than a year ago.

Then, with so many coming off the British and Irish Lions tour of Australia last summer, most had only one game under their belt when looking so flat during their defeat by New Zealand in Chicago. Now, at least, many frontliners have featured in multiple club games before making the jump back to Test-level rugby.

Argentina, however, certainly seem more primed than they have been for recent windows too.

Head coach Felipe Contepomi has spoken of historic significance of chasing a first away win over Ireland, even if 12 of his matchday squad have recent fond memories of the Aviva Stadium from their win over the Lions there 17 months ago.

The side have lost 12 of 18 Tests since that famous win, although Contepomi, like so many of his predecessors, has had difficulties with player availability as a southern hemisphere team whose squad is mainly based in the north.

While there are absentees for this tour - most notably Bath's Santiago Carreras and Lyon prop Thomas Gallo - the 12 changes made from the 28-28 draw with Australia in September undoubtedly have strengthened a starting side with 750 caps' worth of Test experience.

Coupled with the addition of Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma to Contepomi's coaching staff, Los Pumas feel more than capable of giving Ireland exactly the sort of challenge needed as the World Cup looms ever closer on the horizon.

title: Arthur Fils offers injury update after appearing to struggle against Taylor Fritz in Paris
article_text:
Arthur Fils had very little answers to Taylor Fritz in their round of 16 match at the Paris Masters.

The Frenchman fell to a straight sets defeat to the American to end his campaign as his home Masters tournament and he will not turn his attention towards the ATP Finals.

Fils has already confirmed his place at the Turin tournament, although his status looked in doubt as he appeared to struggle in his match against Fritz.

The Frenchman was asked whether he was injured in his post-match press conference at the Paris Masters and he provided a blunt response.

“Tough first question. No, I’m not injured. He was just better than me. I didn’t feel really comfortable on the court because he made me feel like that. He played, I think, a very good match. Congrats to him.”

Fritz produced a very good performance against Fils and the Frenchman was understandably frustrated that he was given little opportunities to shine in front of his home crowd.

“It was very, very complicated, but after all, it’s indoors, so I felt at one point or another, I could have an opportunity. But overall, it’s not that I played badly,” he said.

“It’s just that he played better. He served better, returned better. In the final analysis, it’s two breaks. Not much to say, really.”

Fils was left rueing crucial errors in the match and he will head to the ATP Finals looking to make several improvements for the year-end event.

Yes, there were a number of points where I was too defensive, but it’s a hard court that is extremely fast. We’re not used to playing that fast anymore.

“I could have returned better the second ball, as you said. I could have used my forehand better. Now it’s a bit early. I have to talk to my team. We haven’t debriefed yet, so I have to talk to them to see what parts there are for improvement.”

Despite his round of 16 exit at the Paris Masters, Fils has enjoyed another good season on the ATP Tour, in which he has proved he has all the tools to become one of the very best players in the world.

The Frenchman claimed his maiden Masters title at the Cincinnati Open and he also won the Barcelona Open.

The only disappointing aspect of Fils’ season came at Grand Slam level. He did not play the Australian Open or Roland Garros and he reached the second round of Wimbledon and was knocked out in the first round of the US Open.

title: Korea Open: American Pursuit Gathers Momentum
article_text:
World No.15 Lauren Lam/Allison Quynh Lee continued their march towards a historic breakthrough on Friday, reaching the semifinal of the YEOSU VICTOR Korea Open 2026 with a 21-19 21-10 win over Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva.

The result marks the Americans’ third Super 500 semifinal of the season, adding to a campaign that has also featured a Super 300 semifinal and established them as genuine contenders on the HSBC BWF World Tour.

For a pair seeking to become the first American women’s doubles partnership to win a World Tour title, Yeosu represents another significant step forward. It also comes at an important time for American badminton, with the countdown already under way to the opening of the qualification period for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games next year. With badminton preparing for a rare moment in the spotlight on home soil, Lam/Lee’s continued rise is providing further evidence that the United States can field genuine contenders when qualification begins.

The quarterfinal presented a unique challenge. Across the net stood not only accomplished opponents but close friends and long-time idols.

“It was a fight of the nerves,” Lee told BWF.

Having spent countless hours together on and off court, both pairs entered the quarterfinals with a deep understanding of each other’s strengths and tendencies.

The opening game reflected that familiarity, with neither side able to establish control. Lam/Lee eventually edged ahead at the crucial moments before taking command in the second game to complete a convincing victory.

Lam admitted the emotional aspect of the contest was more difficult before the first shuttle was struck than during the match itself.

“When it was love-all, I was just kind of focused and locked in,” she said. “That feeling just naturally went away.”

The Americans’ rise has not happened overnight. Competing as independent players, they shared the significant sacrifices in pursuit of their ambitions on tour.

“We put everything into this,” Lee said. “We put school on hold. We put on hold on a lot of things, like friendships back at home. We still keep in contact, but obviously we can’t see them all the time, so a lot of sacrifices are put into this, so it does feel really good.”

Their success has also coincided with growing momentum for American badminton across several disciplines.

“I’m really happy that we’re all kind of raising the bar,” Lam said.

Despite another career milestone, neither player is looking beyond the next match.

“We just want to perform well, and then everything else will follow,” Lee said.

That approach has already carried Lam/Lee to another semifinal. Now, with their consistency at Super 500 level becoming impossible to ignore, the prospect of a first World Tour title no longer feels like a distant ambition but an increasingly realistic goal.

They will play Rui Hirokami/Sayaka Hobara for the first time in the semifinals.

title: "Second BWF Title of the Season": Kiren Rijiju Congratulates PV Sindhu on HYLO Open 2026 Triumph
article_text:
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Friday congratulated Indian badminton star PV Sindhu on winning the HYLO Open 2026 in Germany, marking her second title on the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour this season.

Rijiju met the two-time Olympic medallist and her husband, Venkata Datta Sai, and shared a celebratory moment following her victory. He also extended his best wishes to the shuttler for her upcoming tournaments.

"Congratulated @Pvsindhu1 on winning HYLO Open 2026 in Germany! Glad to meet her & Venkata Datta Sai and share the special moment. My best wishes to her for the upcoming tournaments!" Rijiju wrote in a post on X.

Sindhu clinched the women's singles title with a commanding 21-12, 21-14 victory over Denmark's Line Kjaersfeldt in the final.

The Indian shuttler produced a dominant performance in Germany, bouncing back from her runner-up finish at the French Open a week earlier. She had lost the final there to South Korean world number one An Se Young.

In the opening game against Kjaersfeldt, Sindhu made a confident start, although the Danish player initially kept the contest competitive. Kjaersfeldt tested the Indian across the court and brought the score to 5-5 before Sindhu began to take control.

Sindhu entered the interval with an 11-8 advantage and used sharp returns and attacking strokes to widen the gap, eventually closing out the game 21-12.

The second game saw Kjaersfeldt put up a stronger challenge, reducing Sindhu's early 7-3 lead to 7-6. However, the Indian regained control by forcing errors and moving her opponent around the court.

Sindhu led 11-7 at the interval and extended her advantage to 19-11. Despite a late attempt by Kjaersfeldt to narrow the deficit, the Indian held her nerve to seal the match 21-14.

The HYLO Open victory marks Sindhu's second BWF World Tour title of 2026. She had earlier won the Japan Open in July.

The latest triumph comes after an impressive run at the French Open, where she reached the final before losing to An Se Young.

The HYLO Open title adds to Sindhu's growing list of achievements as she continues her campaign on the international badminton circuit.

title: OneCourt, NHL activating through Ticketmaster sponsorship
article_text:
Accessibility tech startup OneCourt and the NHL reached a deal to bring the company’s haptic devices for blind and low-vision fans to the league’s tentpole events. The activation, which comes in collaboration with sponsor Ticketmaster, kicked off at last week’s Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic and will also bring OneCourt to the Discover NHL Winter Classic, Honda NHL All-Star, and Navy Federal Credit Union NHL Stadium Series.

OneCourt -- the Sports Technology of the Year winner at SBA: Tech in May -- has an in-venue product featuring haptics along with a surface that outlines the field of competition. By combining that device with game tracking data, vibrations turn into low-latency play-by-play for users. For NHL games, OneCourt is ingesting the league’s NHL Edge puck- and player-tracking data.

On top of the league connection, the Avalanche, Blackhawks, Capitals and Red Wings will have OneCourt devices at all of their home games this season. Ticketmaster’s sponsorship has helped OneCourt spread throughout professional sports: nine NBA teams deployed OneCourt with the help of the ticketing giant, along with the previously mentioned NHL clubs.

Recently, OneCourt supported games at the FIFA Men’s World Cup and is activating around select Seattle Seahawks games. The 2026 Super Bowl included a OneCourt deployment as well. OneCourt is also producing an at-home device, with an official launch sometime in December.

title: Newmark brings commercial real estate into the Knicks and Rangers sponsorship ecosystem
article_text:
Newmark has entered into a new partnership with two of New York’s most prominent sports franchises, becoming the official commercial real estate partner of the New York Knicks and New York Rangers.

The agreement also extends across the Madison Square Garden portfolio, strengthening the real estate advisory firm’s association with the city’s sports and entertainment industry.

The partnership designates Newmark as an official partner of Madison Square Garden and the official commercial real estate partner of the Westchester Knicks, the NBA G League affiliate of the New York Knicks.

The agreement provides Newmark with a range of branding and promotional opportunities across the franchises and their home venues. These include dasherboard advertising and LED ribbon signage during Knicks and Rangers home games at Madison Square Garden, alongside digitally enhanced dasherboard placements during regular-season home and away games broadcast on MSG Networks.

Newmark will also become the presenting partner of content featured on a Rangers social media platform ahead of every regular-season game. Additional visibility will come through digital signage outside Madison Square Garden and courtside LED advertising during Westchester Knicks home games at the Westchester County Centre.

Doug Jossem, Executive Vice President Global Sports and Entertainment Partnerships, MSG Entertainment, said, “We’re proud to welcome Newmark, one of the world’s foremost commercial real estate firms with deep ties to New York City, to our roster of marketing partners. Bringing together a leading global commercial real estate advisor and service provider and one of the most recognisable sports and entertainment destinations, this partnership delivers meaningful value for both organisations, and we are looking forward to bringing it to life.”

Barry Gosin, Chief Executive Officer of Newmark, added, “Madison Square Garden is one of the most iconic and influential venues in the world, synonymous with excellence, innovation and the energy of New York City. Newmark was founded in Manhattan and is deeply connected to this city’s business community, so we’re proud to partner with an organisation that shares our commitment to excellence, innovation and delivering exceptional experiences.”

The partnership reflects the growing appeal of professional sports properties to business-to-business brands seeking to strengthen corporate relationships and engage with influential audiences. For Newmark, the association provides a platform to reinforce its brand presence across sports, broadcast and digital channels while connecting with the wider New York business ecosystem.

title: Fin Smith fit to face Australia as Ben Curry replaces injured twin Tom in England lineup
article_text:
Fin Smith has successfully come through his final fitness Test to be named at fly-half for England’s autumn opener against Australia while Ben Curry is selected at openside flanker for the first time since the summer of 2025.

Steve Borthwick has made four changes to the side that beat Argentina in July with George Furbank also coming in at fullback, Maro Itoje returning to captain the side and Fin Baxter getting the nod at loosehead prop. The Exeter back-row Greg Fisilau is in line for a debut from the bench.

Smith’s selection is a boost for Borthwick, who lost Tom Curry to an injury sustained in training on Wednesday. The Guardian understands there are concerns that Tom Curry will not be fit to feature at any stage of England’s autumn campaign with twin brother Ben stepping up at openside flanker.

The 24-year-old Smith has started England’s last five matches and has cemented his place as England’s first choice fly-half. Furbank, meanwhile, will make his first appearance for two years as a result of a litany of injuries. He was due to start against South Africa in the summer but was struck down by appendicitis days before the match.

Elsewhere, Itoje comes back into the side after being rested over the summer and takes his place in the second-row alongside Alex Coles. As a result, George Martin must do with a place on the bench, which features a 6-2 split. Baxter’s selection means Ellis Genge is among the replacements to bring ballast from the bench as part of the “Pom Squad”. The Harlequins prop has recovered from a long-term foot injury to make his first appearance since last year’s autumn campaign.

Jack van Poortvliet is picked at scrum-half in the injury absence of Alex Mitchell while Seb Atkinson and Henry Slade reprise their centre partnership. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tommy Freeman continue on the wing. Baxter, Jamie George and Joe Heyes make up the front row while Ollie Chessum and Ben Earl complete the back-row along with Ben Curry.

On the bench, Luke Cowan-Dickie and Will Stuart join Genge in providing front-row back-up while Henry Pollock covers back-row and wing. Ben Spencer and Marcus Smith are the two backs selected among the replacements.

title: Faf de Klerk stood down with immediate effect
article_text:
Faf de Klerk has been ruled out for eight weeks after The Cheetahs confirmed the experienced scrum-half suffered an ankle injury.

The South African was injured during the club's match against Bayonne on October 18 and is expected to return in early January.

The Cheetahs confirmed that De Klerk is targeting a return for their third-round EPCR Challenge Cup clash against Zebre Parma in Italy.

Despite not competing in a European league, the South African side feature in the competition.

De Klerk, who was left out of the Springboks' Nations Championship squad, will be a significant loss for the Cheetahs.

The 35-year-old has won two Rugby World Cups with South Africa, establishing himself as a key figure in their 2019 triumph.

He made his international debut in 2016 before joining Sale Sharks a year later.

De Klerk played a starring role in South Africa's 2019 World Cup campaign, scoring against Japan before starting the final victory over England.

He subsequently moved to Japan's Yokohama Canon Eagles in 2022 before returning to South Africa this year.

His last appearance for the Springboks came against the Barbarians in June, but he has since been overlooked by Rassie Erasmus.

However, the scrum-half has made it clear that his international career is far from over.

De Klerk recently signed a two-year contract with the Cheetahs and has dismissed suggestions that his return to South Africa signals the beginning of retirement.

Despite turning 35 and facing increased competition for the number nine shirt, the experienced scrum-half remains determined to feature at the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

South Africa have considerable depth at scrum-half, with Erasmus giving several players opportunities as he builds towards the tournament.

When De Klerk was omitted earlier this year, the Springboks head coach explained that the decision did not necessarily mark the end of his international career.

Instead, South Africa wanted to assess their other options before finalising their World Cup plans.

That could leave the door open for De Klerk, who played a crucial role in the Springboks' back-to-back World Cup victories in 2019 and 2023.

His immediate focus, however, will be recovering from injury and returning to action with the Cheetahs in January.

title: Former England star set to make Fiji debut after switching international allegiance
article_text:
Former England international Nathan Hughes is set to make his Fiji debut this weekend, seven years after his last appearance for England.

The 35-year-old has been named at number eight for Fiji's Nations Championship clash with France in Lyon on Saturday.

Hughes won 22 caps for England between 2016 and 2019 under Eddie Jones, but will now represent the country of his birth.

The Racing 92 forward will start alongside Pita-Gus Sowakula and Kitione Salawa in Fiji's back row.

Hughes made his England debut against South Africa in November 2016 after impressing for Wasps in the Premiership.

He later played for Bristol Bears and Bath before continuing his career overseas.

Born in Lautoka, Fiji, Hughes qualifies under World Rugby's eligibility regulations, which allow players to switch nations after a three-year stand-down period, subject to birthright requirements and approval.

His return comes under new Fiji head coach Jake White, who has selected the experienced forward for his second match in charge.

Fiji face France on Saturday before taking on Ireland in Dublin on 14 November and Italy the following weekend.

Hughes is one of several players with England experience preparing to represent another nation this autumn.

- 🇹🇴 Manu Vunipola (Tonga): The former England U20 fly-half has been named on Tonga's bench against Romania on Friday. The cousin of Billy and Mako Vunipola could make his senior international debut after completing his switch from England.

- 🇮🇪 Kieran Brookes (Ireland XV): The 36-year-old prop won 16 England caps and featured at the 2015 Rugby World Cup. He has been selected for Ireland XV against Fiji A on 20 November.

- 🇮🇪 Dan Kelly (Ireland XV): The Munster centre won his only England cap against Canada in 2021. He has also been selected for the Fiji A fixture and could push for a place in Ireland's senior squad.

Both Brookes and Kelly have been selected for Ireland's representative XV rather than the senior Test team.

The developments come amid growing uncertainty over the futures of several England-qualified players, with Max Ojomoh also linked with a move away following his latest international snub.
